# metabase_collections (Data Source)

All the Metabase collections visible to the current user.

Along with the attributes returned by the Metabase API, each collection exposes a human-readable `path`, built from the names of its ancestors (e.g. `Marketing/Campaigns`). This makes it possible to look up a collection by the location it has in the interface, rather than by its Metabase ID.

This data source is useful to apply the same configuration to an entire subtree of collections, for example when granting permissions to a collection and all its descendants.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# List all the collections in Metabase.
data "metabase_collections" "all" {}

# The path of a collection is built from the names of its ancestors, which makes it possible to reference a collection
# without knowing its Metabase ID.
output "campaigns_collection_id" {
  value = data.metabase_collections.all.ids_by_path["Marketing/Campaigns"]
}

# Collections can be filtered on their path to apply the same configuration to an entire subtree, for example to grant
# a group access to a collection and all its descendants.
locals {
  marketing_collection_ids = [
    for collection in data.metabase_collections.all.collections :
    collection.id
    if collection.personal_owner_id == null && startswith(collection.path, "Marketing")
  ]
}

output "marketing_collection_ids" {
  value = local.marketing_collection_ids
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `archived` (Boolean) Whether archived collections should be returned instead of active ones. Defaults to `false`.

### Read-Only

- `collections` (Attributes List) The list of collections, sorted by `path`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--collections))
- `ids_by_path` (Map of String) A map where keys are collection `path`s and values are the corresponding collection IDs. When several collections share the same path, only the first one is present in the map and a warning is emitted.

<a id="nestedatt--collections"></a>
### Nested Schema for `collections`

Read-Only:

- `description` (String) A description for the collection.
- `id` (String) The ID of the collection. All user-created collections have an integer ID, the automatically-created root collection's ID is `root`.
- `location` (String) A path-like location, made of the IDs of the ancestors of the collection (e.g. `/12/34/`).
- `name` (String) The name of the collection.
- `parent_id` (Number) The ID of the parent collection. This is null for top-level collections, which belong to the root collection.
- `path` (String) The human-readable path of the collection, made of the names of its ancestors and its own name, separated by `/` (e.g. `Marketing/Campaigns`). The root collection is not part of the path. An ancestor that is not returned by the API is replaced by its ID. Because collection names can themselves contain a `/`, paths are not guaranteed to be unambiguous.
- `personal_owner_id` (Number) The ID of the user owning this collection, if it is a personal collection. This can be used to filter out personal collections.
